mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% within a month indicates a strengthening labor market, which typically boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the unemployment rate decreased by more than 0.3% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP by more than 2% over a quarter signals strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the quarters where real GDP increased by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% within a month signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 70% of the instances where industrial production decreased by more than 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% within a month signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically boosts related sectors and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where housing starts increased by more than 5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.5% within a month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate was above 4% and the consumer price index increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2% within a month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where nonfarm payrolls increased by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreased by more than 0.2% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real retail and food services sales by more than 1% over a quarter signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the quarters where real retail and food services sales increased by more than 1%.
